articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup 2026 Prize Money: How much money players make and what does the winning team get?
articles.standfirst: Team USA is chasing the title, but the financial rewards work very differently from WNBA salaries
articles.summary: Team USA is chasing the title, but the financial rewards work very differently from WNBA salaries
articles.body:
The FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup offers one of the biggest prizes in the sport in terms of prestige, but the financial reward is far less straightforward than the huge prize funds attached to many other major international events.

That matters as Caitlin Clark and Team USA compete on the world stage, because there is no announced FIBA payout guaranteeing players a specific amount simply for winning the tournament.

National-team basketball doesn't operate like the WNBA, where players receive salaries under league contracts.

Instead, compensation is handled largely through individual federations, with travel, accommodation, training and other tournament expenses typically covered while players are with their national teams.

Compensation separate from FIBA prize money

USA Basketball has previously paid women participating in its senior national-team program, but that doesn't mean every international tournament comes with the same guaranteed paycheck.

Ahead of the Tokyo Olympics, USA Basketball introduced a compensation structure that reportedly paid players $2,000 per day while they participated in training camps and games, with additional bonuses possible.

Players who took part throughout the entire program could earn as much as roughly $100,000. Nneka Ogwumike praised that move at the time.

“That investment is what the players want,” Ogwumike said. “It’s quite amazing to afford that type of opportunity. It’s not just about investing in us, but also about the strategic approach of targeting various markets. We’ll have traveling tournaments.”

That marked an important shift in how USA Basketball valued the time commitment required from its women’s national team.

The exact 2026 World Cup compensation structure, however, hasn't been publicly detailed. And there is no confirmed figure showing precisely what Clark or any other Team USA player receives for appearing in the tournament.

What does the Women’s World Cup champion receive?

FIBA hasn't revealed a specific cash prize for the winning team at the 2026 Women’s Basketball World Cup .

That means there is no confirmed championship purse that can be divided among players in the same way prize money is distributed at some tennis, golf or soccer events.

The primary reward remains the title itself, along with the trophy and the status that comes with being crowned world champion.

Any additional financial bonus available to Team USA players would therefore depend on arrangements made by USA Basketball rather than a publicly disclosed FIBA winner’s check.

WNBA salaries remain different financial world

The contrast with the WNBA is significant. Professional league salaries are a player’s primary compensation, while national-team appearances are short-term commitments built around international competition.

In 2025, the WNBA minimum salary was $66,079, while the supermax reached $249,244 and the average salary was reported to be around $120,000.

Those figures could increase substantially under a future collective bargaining agreement, widening the financial gap even further. Representing Team USA, then, isn't primarily about matching WNBA earnings.

The incentive is the chance to win on the international stage, add a world title to a player’s career and compete for one of basketball’s most prestigious trophies.

National-team basketball doesn't operate like the WNBA, where players receive salaries under league contracts.

Instead, compensation is handled largely through individual federations, with travel, accommodation, training and other tournament expenses typically covered while players are with their national teams.
Compensation separate from FIBA prize money
USA Basketball has previously paid women participating in its senior national-team program, but that doesn't mean every international tournament comes with the same guaranteed paycheck.

Players who took part throughout the entire program could earn as much as roughly $100,000. Nneka Ogwumike praised that move at the time.

“That investment is what the players want,” Ogwumike said. “It’s quite amazing to afford that type of opportunity. It’s not just about investing in us, but also about the strategic approach of targeting various markets. We’ll have traveling tournaments.”
That marked an important shift in how USA Basketball valued the time commitment required from its women’s national team.

The exact 2026 World Cup compensation structure, however, hasn't been publicly detailed. And there is no confirmed figure showing precisely what Clark or any other Team USA player receives for appearing in the tournament.
What does the Women’s World Cup champion receive?
FIBA hasn't revealed a specific cash prize for the winning team at the 2026 Women’s Basketball World Cup .
That means there is no confirmed championship purse that can be divided among players in the same way prize money is distributed at some tennis, golf or soccer events.
The primary reward remains the title itself, along with the trophy and the status that comes with being crowned world champion.
Any additional financial bonus available to Team USA players would therefore depend on arrangements made by USA Basketball rather than a publicly disclosed FIBA winner’s check.
WNBA salaries remain different financial world

The contrast with the WNBA is significant. Professional league salaries are a player’s primary compensation, while national-team appearances are short-term commitments built around international competition.
In 2025, the WNBA minimum salary was $66,079, while the supermax reached $249,244 and the average salary was reported to be around $120,000.

Those figures could increase substantially under a future collective bargaining agreement, widening the financial gap even further. Representing Team USA, then, isn't primarily about matching WNBA earnings.
The incentive is the chance to win on the international stage, add a world title to a player’s career and compete for one of basketball’s most prestigious trophies.

articles.summary: The star is spending her break doing what she does best
articles.body:
I t is incredible to see the way Sophie Cunningham has grown and evolved in the basketball world. The player has had several highly criticized moments over the last few months, but she has also produced plenty of viral ones. ​ ​There is a clear divide when it comes to Cunningham’s likability. Some people do not support her at all, while another group simply cannot get enough of her personality.

Sophie’s life away from basketball keeps making headlines

Her break has been anything but quiet. Cunningham has chosen to spend her days with her family and around plenty of animals, who have also become part of her videos . The latest to join Sophie’s viral moments was one of her donkeys.

Cunningham has always embraced country culture and her love for animals. With no teammates around to feature in her videos during the WNBA break, she decided there was no better way to represent the country lifestyle than with a donkey.

Cunningham then took things a step further, casually lying on top of the animal while talking about the country pimp life . The donkey simply stayed still, seemingly unfazed, as the Fever star did her thing and turned it into another completely random Sophie Cunningham moment. The donkey may not have asked for the spotlight, but it certainly became the star of the video.

articles.title: United States: a threatened giant
articles.standfirst: Spain's rival in the World Cup semifinals, a global powerhouse, is the favorite but...
articles.summary: Spain's rival in the World Cup semifinals, a global powerhouse, is the favorite but...
articles.body:
There are stories that can be explained perfectly through the data. The absolute tyranny imposed by the United States women's basketball team is a perfect case. The numbers alone are overwhelming: eight consecutive Olympic golds, four consecutive World Cups as well, almost 20 years without losing a game (the anniversary is on September 21), with a 73-0 record and finishing a World Cup with an average of 40 points ahead of their rivals. No other team sport at the international level, men's or women's, has shown such dominance by one country.

The women's team truly is a Dream Team extended over time. Each team was almost better than the previous one, forming an extraordinary precision machine for playing basketball that hammered the opponent again and again. Fleeting and deadly attacks, unquestionable physicality, a frantic pace and players of enormous quality. An unbroken hegemony... until now.

USA received its first serious warning in the final of the last Games in Paris 2024. An agonizing and, for many, unfair 67-66 victory over France, in a game that the French women knew how to take onto their turf, pulling the giant out of its habitat. They almost won and would have ended 18 years of total dominance.

The Americans escaped that time and also against Italy a few days ago in the 2026 World Cup . Second warning, and this one more serious. France , back then, was another of the favorites at its Games, but Italy was not among the expected medal contenders. The Italians came close , once again bogging the game down, taking the Americans onto the kind of court where they feel most uncomfortable, when they have to extend possessions, which is when the tactical discipline they do not usually have works best. The Europeans were leading with three minutes to go, 51-50, and lost 52-55 in another low-scoring game, with one or two controversial decisions and a three-point attempt at the buzzer by Zandalasini to tie.

These are undeniable signs of weakness, of a fragility they had never shown before. It is a new scenario for players who, for the most part, are still savoring their first sips of international experience. It is a fabulous team when rowing with the wind at its back, it has won many of its games very comfortably in Berlin, but with many doubts and cracks if the wind turns against it. As happened against Italy.

'When the team that would play in the World Cup was made public, experts focused more on the absences: Sabrina Ionescu, Kelsey Plum and, above all, A"ja Wilson . They are tremendous absences, especially Wilson's, the best player on the planet today, the player who, in case of trouble, is always there to take out the trash. That indispensable figure is not on this "Dream Team". '

On the contrary, on the team that is in Berlin many questions have arisen about the performance of some players, especially in close games. Jackie Young is their top scorer, averaging 11, with Napheesa Collier , 9.8, and Breanna Stewart behind her on 9.5. The quality of Caitlin Clark is unquestionable, as is that of Paige Bueckers , but there are many doubts about other players such as Angel Reese, who for many would not have a place if everyone had come, or Chelsea Gray, one of the veterans, but far from her prime.

"But the weakness of the USA is not so much in its play, which remains physical and at times devastating for its rival, as in its chemistry. The team does not seem united, they do not get along well, it is not an environment capable of pushing back against bad moments; on the contrary, they seem to have imported some of the problems hanging over the WNBA itself. If there are problems, they absorb them and create more problems ; they do not repel or solve them. And that disorder is noticeable on the court.

The American team has also shown that it still struggles to adapt to FIBA tournaments. All the teams had their training plan according to the schedules assigned to them , and they followed it. The USA did not like the schedule on a couple of occasions, they gave it up and found themselves an alternative training court . They have repeated it for these semifinals and, on the previous day, they do not train at the Uber Arena. These are the whims of the giant.

Let no one doubt that the USA is still an extraordinary team. It is the favorite against Spain and if it reaches the final, it will be as well. But we must bear in mind that the gaps, which years ago were enormous, have been narrowing, just as is happening in the men's game. After the Berlin World Cup, the hegemony may continue (or not) but what will remain is that teams like France or Spain are starting to get much closer to the giant. It remains to be seen whether close enough to bring it down.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham speaks the truth about what WNBA's next head should change immediately
articles.standfirst: Communication and basic respect must improve when Cathy Engelbert’s successor takes over
articles.summary: Communication and basic respect must improve when Cathy Engelbert’s successor takes over
articles.body:
The WNBA ’s next commissioner will inherit a league with more money, visibility and momentum than at almost any point in its history. Sophie Cunningham believes that will not matter nearly as much as whether the person in charge can actually connect with the players.

With Cathy Engelbert expected to step down at the end of 2026, Cunningham used the debut episode of her new No Hesitation podcast to outline what she wants from the next person in the job.

“It definitely has to be someone who is in great communication with the players because, at the end of the day, we should be joining forces,” Cunningham said.

“We should be working together to grow this league to the best of its ability, and I really do think the sky is the limit when we work together.”

The Indiana Fever guard then described interactions with league leadership that she found far more uncomfortable than confrontational.

“Under previous people who were leading, we would be in the same room with each other… we wouldn’t even say hi, and there would only be like five people in the room,” she said. “Is that not weird or awkward? Just be friendly, just be a human.”

Respect matters more than agreement

Cunningham didn't suggest the commissioner should simply give players whatever they want.

She acknowledged that the WNBA is a business, that ownership groups have invested heavily in its growth and that tension between players and the league office is inevitable.

“I understand that they pretty much work for these billionaires who make a lot of money, and they’ve invested a lot of money in us players and in this league,” Cunningham said.

“And so, we’re not always going to be getting along, but I do think knowing that this new commissioner is going to be for the players and there’s going to be a direct line of communication.”

That distinction is central to her argument. Cunningham appears less concerned with eliminating disagreements than with making sure those disagreements happen inside a relationship built on openness rather than distance.

“We’re not always going to agree, but I think there’s a level of respect that you can have, and just being a human and being friendly and nice,” she added. “I think that’s a really good start.”

Next commissioner inherits both growth and mistrust

Engelbert ’s tenure has coincided with major progress for the WNBA, including rising attendance, stronger television audiences and a significant new media-rights agreement.

At the same time, her relationship with players has repeatedly come under scrutiny.

In 2024, the WNBPA publicly pushed back after Engelbert was criticized for not directly condemning the harassment surrounding the Caitlin Clark - Angel Reese rivalry.

A year later, Napheesa Collier delivered a wider criticism of league leadership over issues including officiating, compensation and communication. Engelbert later acknowledged the problem herself.

“If the players in the ‘W’ don’t feel appreciated and value from the league, we have to do better and I have to do better,” she said.

That leaves the next commissioner with a difficult balance to strike: continuing the league’s commercial rise while repairing trust with the people on the floor.

Cunningham ’s message is that the starting point doesn't need to be complicated. Talk to the players. Respect them. And when they are standing in the same room, at least say hello.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham isn’t hiding: Here’s how she responds to the WNBA’s controversial “sex symbol” label
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever player has turned her pregame looks into part of her image and now explained what’s behind that side of her personality.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever player has turned her pregame looks into part of her image and now explained what’s behind that side of her personality.
articles.body:
There’s something that has become almost as anticipated as watching Sophie Cunningham on the court: finding out what she’ll wear before the next game. The Indiana Fever player often goes for combinations that don’t go unnoticed, from mini shorts and tops to heels and accessories that make her arrival at the arena another moment worth watching.

That fashion choice has become a recognizable part of her presence off the court. But while her outfits may seem spontaneous, Cunningham has a very specific reason for putting so much thought into what she wears before competing , and she explained it herself when she was asked a pretty direct question.

The question that put “sex symbol” on the table

The topic came up during an interview with Colin Cowherd , who asked Cunningham directly whether it was fair to consider her the “sex symbol” of the WNBA .

The question could have taken the conversation in any direction, but Sophie chose to explain what the attention she receives for her appearance and the way she dresses means to her.

Her answer began with something more personal than might have been expected: she has always been very feminine .

Cunningham explained that she has loved dresses, heels and getting dressed up since she was a little girl. To her, that part of her personality doesn’t disappear when she steps onto a basketball court .

Sophie Cunningham doesn’t think she has to choose between being feminine and competing

That’s where one of the most interesting ideas in her response comes in. Sophie doesn’t believe there is only one right way to be an athlete.

She can dress in a very feminine way and then step onto the court and compete with intensity. She could also choose a more masculine style and still be exactly the same player .

That combination is precisely what she wants to show: one thing doesn’t cancel out the other.

That perspective also helps explain why her looks don’t seem like a separate character from the athlete who appears on the court moments later. For Cunningham, both sides are simply part of who she is .

But there was another reason she has embraced the attention.

There’s also a business side to Sophie Cunningham’s image

The player acknowledged that there are now plenty of eyes on everything they do, and that’s where her entrepreneurial side comes in.

If people are paying attention to what she wears, Cunningham understands that attention can also become an opportunity . It’s not just about choosing an outfit she likes, but recognizing the value an image can have when there is an audience interested in seeing it.

That approach has already taken a concrete form beyond her pregame appearances.

This summer, the Adidas Crazy Energy “Sophie Cunningham” PE went on sale , an exclusive player edition based on an existing basketball silhouette from the brand. In this case, “PE” stands for Player Exclusive, meaning it is a personalized version made for her rather than an entirely new signature line .

So what starts with a look before walking into the arena can end up taking on a much bigger dimension.

Her look doesn’t change what Sophie Cunningham brings on the court

All of this is happening as Cunningham goes through an important season with Indiana. In 2026, she is averaging 8.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game, along with 22.7 minutes per game across 39 appearances .

The WNBA is currently on a break for the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup , but the wait is almost over. The regular season will resume on September 17, while the Indiana Fever will return to the court on September 18 against Toronto Tempo .

And when Sophie Cunningham shows up before a game again, there will probably be two things drawing attention: what she does on the court and, once again, what she decided to wear to get there.

articles.title: Where does Angel Reese’s fashion style come from? Her mom might have the answer
articles.standfirst: An Angel post put her mom back in front of the camera, and her look ended up offering a clue about a passion the player has carried with her since childhood.
articles.summary: An Angel post put her mom back in front of the camera, and her look ended up offering a clue about a passion the player has carried with her since childhood.
articles.body:
There’s something that happens when a fashion star lets her mom step into the spotlight: suddenly, you start looking at the details differently. That’s what happened with Angel Reese, who shared a video on Instagram featuring Angel Webb Reese , and this time, it was her mom’s outfit that ended up stealing some of the attention.

It wasn’t a runway look, nor did it need to be. A printed white T-shirt, capri pants, black flip-flops, sunglasses, a light denim jacket and a black Chanel bag were enough to leave one question hanging in the air: what if Angel Reese’s good taste didn’t come out of nowhere?

The coincidence is especially interesting when you remember that Angel has been interested in fashion since she was a child.

Before the tunnel fits, there was mom’s closet

Long before the big designers, cameras and tunnel fits, Angel already had one of the most classic activities for any girl curious about clothes: exploring her mom’s closet .

In some interviews, Angel has said that she was drawn to the fashion world from a young age. Like many girls, she found in that space a way to explore, try different styles and discover which pieces caught her attention . Today, that childhood curiosity looks very different when you consider everything she has built around her personal style.

Because fashion didn’t enter her life when the spotlight arrived. It was already there.

From playing with clothes to becoming a model

Her looks have included brands such as Chanel and Louis Vuitton , along with jewelry from Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels . She has also appeared in Vogue and at events such as the Met Gala , while her appearance at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show took that side of her career even further.

For that runway, she even worked with a modeling instructor beforehand to perfect her walk.

The transformation is interesting precisely because of that: the girl who was once curious about clothes eventually turned fashion into an important part of how she presents herself to the world.

And now her mom appears in a video, carrying a Chanel bag and putting together a look that shows a love for dressing well doesn’t necessarily stay outside the home, either.

And while all this is happening, Angel keeps shining.

How is she doing at the World Cup?

The post also arrives at an important moment for Reese. The player is still competing with the United States at the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup in Berlin , where the team advanced undefeated to the semifinals and will face Spain this Saturday, September 12.

Reese enters that matchup averaging 8.8 points and 6.0 rebounds per game, along with 1.5 steals and 1.0 blocks . Her 63.2% field-goal percentage makes her the tournament leader in that category, according to the data provided.

After the World Cup, her schedule will shift back to the WNBA: the Atlanta Dream are scheduled to return on Thursday, September 17, against the Connecticut Sun .

But for now, between one game and the next, an apparently simple post left something else on the table. Angel Reese may have her own fashion language today, but when you look at the woman who was at home before all those spotlights, the connection is too curious to ignore.

articles.summary: A photo of the Indiana Fever star with a mystery man sparked immediate speculation about her private life
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has found herself at the center of a new wave of attention away from basketball after a photo claiming to show her with a possible new boyfriend began circulating online.

The Indiana Fever guard appeared alongside a man in an image that quickly spread across social media, with fans immediately trying to determine whether Cunningham had quietly entered a new relationship.

For now, there has been no confirmation that Cunningham is in a new relationship, and the viral image alone doesn't establish one.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham shuts down Enes Kanter Freedom partnership: “I’m just focused on the Fever”
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star has found herself linked to Enes Kanter Freedom's controversial WNBA campaign, but she is making it clear that her priorities remain firmly with her team
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star has found herself linked to Enes Kanter Freedom's controversial WNBA campaign, but she is making it clear that her priorities remain firmly with her team
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has delivered a simple response to the latest controversy surrounding her name: she does not intend to get involved.

The Indiana Fever forward has become an increasingly prominent voice in the wider discussion surrounding transgender participation in women's sports.

Her previous comments on the subject subsequently attracted the attention of former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White , who have attempted to turn the WNBA into a stage for their own protest.

But while Kanter Freedom has repeatedly praised Cunningham and portrayed her as an important supporter of his position, Cunningham herself appears unwilling to become associated with his campaign.

Asked by ESPN about the two former NBA players declaring their intentions to enter the WNBA, Cunningham refused to make the situation a bigger part of her own story.

“I'm gonna let them do them,” Cunningham told ESPN. “I'm just focused on the Fever and on our sport. I think we have four more games left. I'm trying to just really dial in and keep the main thing the main thing.”

That response comes at an important point in Indiana's season.

With only four regular-season games remaining, Cunningham's attention is understandably turning toward the Fever's playoff ambitions rather than an off-court political dispute.

The team has also publicly backed her for Sixth Player of the Year, highlighting her career-best shooting numbers and contribution to its season.

Cunningham is averaging 8.3 points per game while shooting 46.9% from the field and 43.4% from three-point range, according to the Fever's own campaign for the award.

That makes her decision to concentrate on basketball particularly understandable.

Kanter Freedom has repeatedly brought Cunningham into the controversy

The connection between Cunningham and Kanter Freedom intensified following his appearance at the Fever's August 23 game against the Chicago Sky .

Kanter Freedom was ejected from the contest after a confrontation involving Sky guard Natasha Cloud. He later claimed that Cunningham had reached out to him afterward.

“What happened?” she asked, according to Kanter Freedom.

The former NBA player subsequently spoke extremely positively about Cunningham , describing her as someone who was willing to challenge the WNBA publicly.

“She's standing for the truth… I think she's an idol now and an American hero,” Kanter Freedom said. “I'm just really happy that finally someone from the WNBA got up and said, 'Enough is enough. We have to stand for American values.”

Kanter Freedom 's actions at the Chicago game became part of the controversy themselves. He wore a T-shirt displaying the words:

“Woman. Noun,” it read. “Adult human female.”

The former NBA center maintained that he had not broken the league's Fan Code of Conduct. He argued that he had simply been celebrating a Cunningham three-pointer when he stood up and raised his arms.

He later escalated the dispute by filing a federal lawsuit against the Chicago Sky, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority and the City of Chicago, arguing that he had been improperly removed from the arena.

In announcing the lawsuit on X, Kanter Freedom wrote: “SEE YOU IN COURT!!! Just filed a federal complaint. I'm taking legal action over my ejection from the @ChicagoSky game while peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights.

“My T-shirt did what the whole @WNBA apparently couldn't: define a woman. No threats. No violence. Just biology. And somehow, that required a security escort. You don't have to agree with my speech but you don't get to silence me for it.

“I will not be intimidated. I will not be silenced. I will continue to stand for women and defend free speech.”

Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter responded by describing the lawsuit as 'meritless and frivolous' and saying he would 'look forward to the truth prevailing in court.'

The Cunningham connection has also been complicated by the involvement of Royce White .

White, another former NBA player who has since entered politics, appeared at a Fever game wearing a long blonde wig as part of his attempt to draw attention to his proposed WNBA entry. His appearance was presented as another challenge to the league's rules and sparked further discussion around Cunningham's earlier comments.

However, Cunningham's latest comments suggest she does not intend to become a participant in the publicity campaign.

That distinction is important because Kanter Freedom has made her comments a recurring part of his argument, while Cunningham is now attempting to move the conversation back toward the court.

Her recent activities also suggest that basketball is becoming an increasingly important focus away from game nights. Cunningham has launched a new podcast, No Hesitation, with basketball trainer Drew Hanlen, replacing her previous show with West Wilson. She has said the new project will concentrate more heavily on basketball and the WNBA.

That shift fits with the message she delivered to ESPN.

Whatever Cunningham's personal views on the underlying debate, she is drawing a boundary between expressing her own opinion and publicly supporting Kanter Freedom or White's campaign.

For the Fever, there is also a much more immediate objective.

Indiana is heading into the final stretch of the regular season, with Cunningham playing an important role off the bench and the organization publicly promoting her award credentials. With the postseason approaching, there is little time for distractions.

Kanter Freedom and White may continue trying to use the WNBA as a platform for their campaign, and Cunningham's earlier remarks may remain part of that conversation. But Cunningham's position now appears straightforward.

She is not volunteering to become the face of their movement, nor is she publicly endorsing their tactics. Instead, with the Fever's season entering its decisive phase, she wants the discussion to return to basketball.

As she put it: “I'm just focused on the Fever and on our sport.” For Cunningham, that appears to be where the attention will stay.

articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham may have found her next competition, and fans are already making their pitch
articles.body:
Some Sophie Cunningham fans still cannot get over the Indiana Fever star not being selected to represent Team USA at the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup. Now, they are already thinking about what could be the next big move for Cunningham.

With her Indiana Fever colors back on, Sophie is getting ready for her teammates to return from Germany so they can get back to training and playing together. In a TikTok featuring some playful moves, Cunningham gave fans a glimpse of her energy away from the court, and it immediately sparked a new idea.

Fans already have a new challenge in mind

The idea of seeing Cunningham compete in a different setting outside basketball is tempting , and fans are making sure she knows it. Comments on her videos have turned into a full-on push for Sophie to consider joining Dancing With The Stars .

Just imagining Cunningham bringing her competitiveness, fierceness and passion to a dance floor is enough for fans to believe it could be iconic. The possibility has already become difficult for them to ignore.

The fandom is ready to show up

The moves might need a little polish, but the rhythm is there. More importantly, fans believe Cunningham already has the competitive mentality and the support needed to make a run on the show . They are convinced her fandom would be one of the biggest and most unbreakable in the competition.

This is only a tempting request from fans . As far as we know, Cunningham has not received a formal invitation to join the next season of the competition, but fans would love to see the idea become a reality, and even thinking about it has them excited . For now, they will have to settle for watching Cunningham dance on TikTok and come up with more playful choreographies. But if the fan movement keeps growing, that invitation could arrive sooner than expected.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark vs Angel Reese: one wins in playmaking, the other rules the boards, Who was the best at the World Cup?
articles.standfirst: Both were champions and have been compared for years since their college showdown in 2023. Now, as United States teammates, the World Cup makes it possible to measure their performance on the same team for the first time
articles.summary: Both were champions and have been compared for years since their college showdown in 2023. Now, as United States teammates, the World Cup makes it possible to measure their performance on the same team for the first time
articles.body:
"C aitlin Clark and Angel Reese finished their World Cup debut with a gold medal and, this time, sharing a locker room although with different roles within the United States team.

The 97-79 victory over France made the U.S. women's team champions for the fifth consecutive time, and both Caitlin and Angel had to adapt to a secondary role and as support players since they shared the team with great veterans and renowned players.

A rivalry that was born in the NCAA and continues in the WNBA

Both made it to the United States national team after a rivalry that began in the NCAA and continued in the WNBA, but the Berlin championship offered a different setting: to measure what each contributed to the same team.

point guard for the United States, with 5.8 assists per game, while Reese finished as the team's second-best rebounder, with 5.4 boards, and added 0.8 blocks and 1.2 steals per game. They did not contribute the same things, but the numbers make it possible to identify where each one's advantage lay.

Clark won the creation duel

Averaging 5.8 assists, Caitlin led the United States in that statistic . In the quarterfinals against Hungary, she delivered one of her best games of the tournament: 10 points and nine assists in the 108-56 victory.

Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese finished the FIBA World Cup averaging 7.2 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.2 steals, and 0.8 blocks (the team's best mark) in six games played.

She also played a key role in the comeback in the final. France led by 14 points during the second quarter, but Clark closed the first half with a three-pointer that left the United States just two points behind. She finished the game with 12 points, although she also lost four balls and received a technical.

Reese, more weight in rebounding and defense

In the quarterfinals against Hungary, Reese finished with 9 points and six rebounds, while Clark recorded 10 points and nine assists.

Reese's best performance came in the group stage against the Czech Republic , in which she scored 13 points, grabbed six rebounds, and stole three balls, contributing to the United States' emphatic 105-64 victory.

However, although Reese proved at the World Cup to be one of the best defensive players in women’s basketball today, she did not win the award for Best Defensive Player of the tournament . Instead, the honor went to the French point guard and Golden State Valkyries All-Star, Gabby Williams .

If the comparison focuses on the statistical weight within the construction of the offense, the advantage goes to Clark . Her 5.8 assists per game were a standout figure within the United States team, and her ability to create shots for her teammates was especially valuable on a team with numerous scorers. Reese, on the other hand, had a greater impact on rebounding and defensive statistics.

If you have to choose between the two taking their statistical impact at the World Cup as a reference, Clark comes out slightly ahead because of her playmaking ability. Reese posted better numbers in rebounds, steals, and blocks, but the point guard's contribution carried greater weight in the champion's offensive creation.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham’s football kick goes wrong in front of hundreds at NASCAR race
articles.standfirst: Sophie Cunningham brought her athletic skills to NASCAR, but her football attempt did not go as planned
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham brought her athletic skills to NASCAR, but her football attempt did not go as planned
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham made her presence felt at the NASCAR Cup Series race. The Indiana Fever star was in Madison, Illinois, for Sunday’s Enjoy Illinois 300, and she hardly stayed in the background . But a moment on stage quickly became the highlight of her visit for a very different reason, as her athleticism did not exactly shine during a football kicking attempt.

Cunningham is known as a basketball player, but she also has experience with football. She stepped in as a kicker in high school after a teammate was injured and took over the role. It is possible she has not practiced those skills since then, and her attempt at the NASCAR event showed some of that rust.

Sophie wanted to put her football skills on display

Cunningham lined up to kick the football in front of the crowd, taking the challenge seriously. She even took off her shoes and took a run-up to get the right approach before making her attempt.

Things quickly went wrong . Instead of sending the football where she intended, Cunningham kicked it directly into a nearby tripod and microphone, sending the equipment crashing off the stage. The chaotic moment instantly looked like a meme, but Cunningham took the mishap with humor.

Cunningham had more than one role at the race

Cunningham was in Madison for the Enjoy Illinois 300 and spent time around the NASCAR garage and pre-race festivities. T he WNBA guard also crossed paths with some of the biggest names in the sport and tried her hand at kicking a football into the crowd, although that part did not go according to plan.

The Missouri native was also set to contribute to USA Network’s race broadcast, giving her trip to Gateway a role beyond that of a celebrity guest. Her football kick may not have gone the way she wanted, but it certainly made her presence at the race memorable.

articles.title: Why Was Caitlin Clark Punished in the Middle of the World Cup Final? Her Reaction Said It All
articles.standfirst: The NBA star was at the center of a tense moment during the 2026 FIBA World Cup final between the United States and France.
articles.summary: The NBA star was at the center of a tense moment during the 2026 FIBA World Cup final between the United States and France.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark expressed her disbelief at one of the most unexpected moments of the Women’s Basketball World Cup final. With Team USA on its way to victory over France, the Indiana Fever star received a technical foul that left her completely bewildered.

The episode takes on special significance because the Indiana Fever guard had already accumulated several technical fouls during the WNBA season. One of them was later rescinded by the league, avoiding an automatic suspension.

The sanction was Clark's first technical foul during the tournament

The Team USA star received a technical foul against France and could not hide her disbelief. The situation occurred in the fourth quarter, when United States was leading 73-57. Clark had just been called for an offensive foul and, after the whistle, remained holding the ball in her hands.

The decision took the player by surprise, and she immediately turned toward the referees with an expression of disbelief. According to the match footage, Clark repeated the same question with her lips: “For what?” , making it clear that she did not understand the reason for the penalty.

At first it seemed like she was going to slam it against the floor out of frustration, but in the end she did not and handed it to the referee. Even so, the officials decided to penalize her with a technical foul.

This was the first technical foul she received during the World Cup, and it did not end up having a decisive impact on the final result.

The United States came back from a 14-point deficit and defeated France 97-79 to claim its fifth consecutive World Cup and twelfth in history, and at the time of the incident it was already on a considerable sale,

Clark contributed 12 points and three assists, including a decisive three-pointer near the end of the first half that allowed the Americans to go into the break trailing by only two points. Breanna Stewart was Team USA’s leading scorer with 22 points and 10 rebounds.

Thus Caitlin's team won the gold medal for the fifth consecutive year and the NBA star celebrated alongside her teammates.

The technical foul episode, however, remained one of the most striking scenes of the night. As the United States moved toward celebrating the title, Clark was still trying to understand a refereeing decision that, judging by her reaction, she clearly did not expect.

articles.title: Who is Sophie Cunningham’s alleged new boyfriend? A photo may have revealed him
articles.standfirst: A photo of the Indiana Fever star alongside a man sparked questions during the WNBA break, but his identity makes the story even more intriguing.
articles.summary: A photo of the Indiana Fever star alongside a man sparked questions during the WNBA break, but his identity makes the story even more intriguing.
articles.body:
The WNBA was on a break for several days because of the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup , and Sophie Cunningham took advantage of that time away from the court. But even though she was not playing, her name resurfaced on social media for a completely different reason.

One photo was enough to spark questions

An X account called Fever Updates shared a split photo in which Cunningham appears in a bikini alongside a man.

In one part, the two smile at the camera . In the other, Sophie leans on the man’s shoulder while he looks at her . He is wearing a black life jacket with red details and a black cap, while the player is wearing a two-piece bikini.

And that is when the inevitable question began: who is he?

There is something important to clarify before going any further. The photos have started circulating now , but that does not establish when they were taken. Sophie has also not publicly confirmed a romantic relationship with the man pictured alongside her.

But his identity is certainly intriguing.

The man several reports identify as Frank Adams currently works in college basketball. He is the head athletic trainer for Grand Canyon University’s men’s basketball team in Arizona .

His career is far from small, either. Before joining Grand Canyon, Adams spent six years as an assistant athletic trainer for the Phoenix Suns , where he worked with NBA players on treatments and individualized care plans.

Before that, he was the head athletic trainer for the Iowa Wolves, an NBA G League team.

And it is precisely his time in Phoenix that gives this story an even more interesting connection to Sophie.

Did Sophie and Frank already know each other?

Sophie Cunningham spent six seasons with the Phoenix Mercury before being traded to the Indiana Fever in February 2025 .

At the same time, Adams was working with the Phoenix Suns.

That means the two were professionally connected to Phoenix basketball for several years. However, there is not enough information to say that they met there, so that possibility should remain exactly that: a possibility .

What it does explain is why Frank Adams is not a name completely disconnected from Sophie’s basketball world.

And while the photos continue to fuel speculation, Cunningham’s dating history also helps explain why the appearance of a new man by her side attracted so much attention .

Sophie has kept her love life mostly away from the court

Sophie’s last publicly known relationship was with Jakob Neidig , whom she began dating in 2019 while they were both student-athletes at the University of Missouri .

During that time, their relationship was visible on social media. Neidig even appeared supporting Sophie during her games, and the two shared photos together.

The relationship ended around 2020 , and since then, Cunningham has kept much more privacy around her love life.

That is why a photo like this has a different effect. Not because it confirms that Frank is her partner , but because it puts a new face at the center of a conversation Sophie does not usually fuel publicly.

Meanwhile, Sophie is getting ready to return

All of this comes as Cunningham is having a solid season with the Indiana Fever.

During the 2026 season, Sophie is averaging 8.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game .

Her next game is scheduled for September 18, when Indiana visits the Toronto Tempo.

articles.standfirst: Somebody get Caitlin Clark some goggles, because Team USA’s gold medal celebration got a little painful
articles.summary: Somebody get Caitlin Clark some goggles, because Team USA’s gold medal celebration got a little painful
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark is known for being one of the most skilled players on the court, but one move during the FIBA Women’s World Cup showed that she does not always have every move under control. ​Clark is also known for having fun, especially when things go her way. Much has been said about the unity of the United States team, with the players making it clear that they are not only teammates but friends.

Team USA had plenty to celebrate

The chemistry between the players helped them secure the victory, and after a well-executed tournament , champagne had to be part of the celebration. With Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers also part of the team, the TikToks were always going to be part of the party, especially after winning gold.

Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and the rest of the championship squad popped champagne and celebrated together. While the final score was one-sided, Team USA first had to overcome a 14-point deficit in the first half. The Americans had erased most of it by halftime but still trailed by three at the break. A 30-12 run in the third quarter then removed any doubt and secured the United States’ fifth straight World Cup title.

Clark’s champagne move did not go as planned

That was when the celebration really began, with Clark joining her teammates to enjoy the victory. Reese organized the team for a TikTok that left fans with a moment to remember. T he only thing they forgot to bring was a good pair of goggles to protect themselves from the champagne.

Luckily for fans, Reese posted the video of the team celebrating, with Clark taking charge of shaking the champagne bottl e. She was so excited that t he champagne went straight into her own eyes, and the entire moment was caught on camera.

Fans and supporters quickly joined the online conversation with humorous reactions to the unfiltered celebration. Even Clark’s boyfriend, Connor McCaffery, joined in by reposting the amusing footage on his social media story .

articles.standfirst: Following her gold medal win with Team USA, Clark's next game is with the Fever on Friday
articles.summary: Following her gold medal win with Team USA, Clark's next game is with the Fever on Friday
articles.body:
For a fifth consecutive tournament and seven of the last eight iterations, Team USA captured the gold medal at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup after dismantling France 97-79 behind a stellar 30-12 third-quarter onslaught, bouncing back brilliantly after facing a one-point deficit at halftime.

Throughout the final clash and the broader tournament stretch, the Americans were driven by Breanna Stewart , who closed out the championship game with 22 points and 10 rebounds . With this latest triumph, Stewart etched her name in history by becoming the first player to earn multiple MVP honors (2018, 2026) while securing her fourth Women’s World Cup gold medal.

Caitlin Clark Shines on International Stage Ahead of Nike Shoe Launch

Beyond Stewart's dominant MVP campaign, Caitlin Clark cemented her status as a vital engine for the red, white, and blue, averaging 7.0 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 5.8 assists per game while pacing the entire tournament with 32 total assists across 6 matches , highlighted by an incredible 11 assists during her opening-round debut against China .

With international play concluded, Clark and her peers immediately pivot back to the WNBA, which resumes this Thursday with all 15 league teams facing a four-game sprint to wrap up the regular season, even as the eight postseason teams have already locked up their playoff bids.

Adding to the massive wave of momentum surrounding her return, Clark is officially gearing up to launch her highly anticipated inaugural signature footwear line with Nike .

The sportswear giant announced that the Nike Caitlin 1 will officially debut globally on October 1 via Nike.com and select stockists, accompanied by an expansive 18-piece apparel collection.

Responding to the official reveal on social media with an energetic tease, "We are very close" , fans instantly began speculating whether the timeline aligns seamlessly with a deep postseason run.

Engineered directly from strict performance metrics demanded by Clark herself, the new signature silhouette focuses heavily on three core functional goals: executing a quicker first step, generating more separation on a faster step-back, and achieving a faster shot release.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese having lunch together after winning the FIBA World Cup? Here's what we know about the viral photo
articles.standfirst: A viral image claimed Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese shared a lunch in Europe after winning the FIBA World Cup.
articles.summary: A viral image claimed Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese shared a lunch in Europe after winning the FIBA World Cup.
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark and Angel Reese were key figures in Team USA’s championship run at the FIBA Women’s World Cup , where they shared a locker room and helped the team capture the gold medal.

With the WNBA set to resume action on Thursday, both stars still have a few days off before returning to their respective teams. However, a viral image on social media has sparked conversation after claiming the two shared a moment together following the championship.

Viral post claims Clark and Reese had lunch together

A post on X began circulating quickly after claiming that Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese were seen having lunch together in Europe following their FIBA World Cup triumph . The image shows both stars sitting at a restaurant table, apparently sharing a meal and smiling during the encounter.

The message accompanying the photo read:

“After winning the FIBA World Cup, Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese were spotted together enjoying a European lunch.”

However, several elements in the image raise questions about its authenticity. The photo shows a sign with the words “Greenwich Village,” a reference associated with New York and not a location in Europe .

Additionally, there are no credible reports confirming that Clark and Reese had lunch together after the tournament, while their public activity does not support that version of events.

In an era where artificial intelligence is capable of creating increasingly realistic images, everything indicates that the viral photo could be digitally generated or manipulated content.

Clark and Reese celebrate world championship

Clark and Reese were part of the United States team that faced France in the FIBA Women’s World Cup final on Sunday in Berlin, Germany , where the Americans captured the gold medal.

Reese shared a championship celebration message after the victory, while Clark’s latest Instagram post around that time focused on her signature Nike Caitlin 1 sneakers .

Following the win, Clark was also asked about her relationship with Reese. During the postgame press conference, a reporter asked whether the two were now “friends.”

The Indiana Fever star responded:

“We’ve always been friends. Don’t try to do that,” while pointing toward the reporter.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham reveals talks with Adam Silver on WNBA Commissioner search
articles.standfirst: Cunningham says the league needs a commissioner who can unite players and continue its rapid growth
articles.summary: Cunningham says the league needs a commissioner who can unite players and continue its rapid growth
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has revealed that she’s spoken with NBA commissioner Adam Silver about the search for the next leader of the WNBA , offering a glimpse into what she hopes the league’s next chapter will look like.

The Indiana Fever guard said Silver reached out to her and that the pair have spoken several times.

Although Cunningham didn’t reveal specific details about the candidates being considered, she praised Silver’s knowledge and said his perspective gave her valuable insight into the direction of the search.

“He was very knowledgeable and full of wisdom and so getting to talk to him and hear his perspective of how he approaches the NBA is huge, who he's kind of looking for,” said Cunningham .

“I think if you want to know the real answers, you go to him. But I think he's going to put someone in place who really wants to take our league to another level than it's already at.

“Our league is booming, so why would we not (want) someone who's going to make it even more booming?”

Cathy Engelbert, who has served as commissioner since 2019, is set to leave her position at the end of the year after overseeing a period of significant expansion for the league.

The WNBA has experienced substantial increases in attention, television audiences, ticket demand and merchandise sales in recent seasons. The arrival of Caitlin Clark, who was selected first overall by Indiana in 2024, has further accelerated the league’s growing popularity.

Cunningham wants a leader who can unite the WNBA

The Fever guard believes the league needs a commissioner who can bring together players, teams and fans despite their differences.

“But I do think with that you need someone who's going to unite everybody because it can be so different. But that doesn't mean it's a bad thing. I think it makes it a lot of fun,” said Cunningham.

Cunningham has become a controversial figure because of her outspoken views on transgender participation in women’s sports, which have generated both support and criticism.

Despite that controversy, she says the diversity of opinions and backgrounds within the WNBA can be one of its greatest strengths. She wants the league’s next leader to recognize those differences while creating a sense of common purpose.

Cunningham acknowledged that the commissioner ultimately works on behalf of the league’s owners and will sometimes have to make difficult decisions that players don’t agree with.

articles.standfirst: The clip gained traction online because it involved two of the biggest stars in women's basketball
articles.summary: The clip gained traction online because it involved two of the biggest stars in women's basketball
articles.body:
T he United States women's basketball team left Germany with another gold medal, but one of the most talked-about moments from its FIBA World Cup run had nothing to do with the final score. Instead, it came from a brief interaction between Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese that quickly made the rounds on social media.

In a video posted on X, Clark appeared ready to receive the ball from Reese during a Team USA sequence. When the pass never came, Clark was left momentarily waiting before responding in a way that had fans laughing. Rather than showing frustration, the Indiana Fever star appeared to playfully acknowledge the moment, turning what could have been an awkward sequence into a lighthearted exchange.

The clip gained traction online because it involved two of the biggest stars in women's basketball, whose every interaction tends to attract attention.

Clark and Reese frequently displayed strong chemistry

For years, Clark and Reese have been linked by one of the sport's most discussed rivalries. From their memorable NCAA Tournament battles to their WNBA matchups, fans have scrutinized nearly every on-court exchange between the two stars.

But Team USA's run at the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup offered a very different picture. Throughout the tournament, Clark and Reese frequently displayed strong chemistry while helping the Americans capture a fifth consecutive World Cup title. Reese publicly praised the opportunity to play alongside Clark , while Caitlin pushed back against narratives suggesting the two have personal issues.

Following the championship victory over France, Clark even dismissed a reporter's attempt to create controversy, saying, "We've always been friends. Don't try to do that." That context made the viral video all the more entertaining.

The moment showcased the comfort level that appears to have developed between the two young stars and some of the biggest WNBA names. Clark's reaction suggested she understood exactly what had happened and decided to have fun with it.

The timing also added another layer to the story

Team USA was in the middle of a remarkable championship run that concluded with a 97-79 victory over France in the gold-medal game. The Americans extended their World Cup dominance with a 36th consecutive tournament victory dating back to 2006.

Breanna Stewart led the way with 22 points in the final and earned tournament MVP honors, while Clark contributed 12 points as the Americans pulled away in the second half. France briefly led by 14 points before the United States stormed back and reasserted its dominance.

The tournament represented a significant milestone. Although veterans like Stewart carried much of the scoring load, the younger generation gained valuable experience while helping Team USA maintain its status as the gold standard of international women's basketball.

Moments like the viral Clark-Reese clip also highlighted something else: how much public perception of their relationship has evolved. Earlier in their careers, nearly every interaction between the two generated debate. During this tournament, however, fans saw numerous examples of cooperation, communication, and even humor between the pair.

articles.title: Adam Silver’s private call to Sophie Cunningham reveals how powerful her voice has become
articles.standfirst: The Fever guard was already one of the WNBA’s most visible and polarizing players, but nobody knew the NBA commissioner was listening to her
articles.summary: The Fever guard was already one of the WNBA’s most visible and polarizing players, but nobody knew the NBA commissioner was listening to her
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has attracted attention for refusing to back down, protecting her teammates and playing every possession with an edge. Her basketball ability, athletic figure and growing media presence have also made her one of the WNBA’s most recognizable players.

What nobody knew was that her voice had become important enough for NBA commissioner Adam Silver to call her privately.

Cunningham revealed that she has spoken with Silver “a couple times” about the future of the WNBA and the search for Cathy Engelbert’s replacement. Silver reportedly contacted Cunningham through a connection with her agents, who are close to the commissioner.

Why did Adam Silver call Sophie Cunningham?

There is no public evidence that Cunningham and Silver are personal friends. Their relationship appears to be professional, but the conversation shows how much her influence has grown. Cunningham is no longer simply the fearless Fever player who became famous for defending Caitlin Clark. She has become one of the league’s loudest and most closely watched voices.

Neither side has revealed everything that was said. The NBA declined to discuss the conversation, while Cunningham offered one intriguing answer: “If you want to know the real answers, you go to him.”

She did reveal what she wants from the next WNBA commissioner: someone who puts players first, communicates with them and can unite a league filled with different personalities and beliefs. She also believes Silver wants a leader capable of taking the WNBA’s explosive growth to another level.

Cunningham did not name a preferred candidate, and it remains unclear whether Silver directly asked her to choose one. But the call itself may say more than any name could. One of basketball’s most powerful executives wanted to hear what she thought and Sophie Cunningham now has his ear.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham turned her back on Caitlin Clark after blunt response according to fans
articles.standfirst: Her four-word answer left fans questioning her support for her Fever teammates
articles.summary: Her four-word answer left fans questioning her support for her Fever teammates
articles.body:
I t is not new for Sophie Cunningham to find herself at the center of controversy. However, this latest situation caught fans off guard , especially because of the perception that she showed little interest in what her Indiana Fever teammates and friends , Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston, accomplished on the other side of the world.

Some fans suggested Cunningham’s response made her look resentful about not being selected to represent Team USA at the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup. Her game and popularity have continued to grow in recent years, with some fans even questioning why she was not considered for the roster , while others argued there were other players who deserved the spot ahead of her .

A response that caught fans off guard

The situation came after a reporter asked Cunningham if she had watched the World Cup final to see her Fever teammates Clark and Boston compete for Team USA. Cunningham said she had not watched the game because she was busy, but the attitude behind the brief response was what drew attention from fans.

The gold-medal game between the United States and France took place at 2 p.m. ET on Sunday. Around that same time, Cunningham was making an appearance at NASCAR’s Enjoy Illinois 300 in Madison, Illinois, giving context to why she may not have been able to watch the game.

Fans question the support between teammates

The criticism came quickly, with fans describing Cunningham’s answer as a sour response , especially given how close she is with Clark and Boston. Her blunt reaction left some questioning why she appeared so indifferent toward two of her Fever teammates and friends.

Others, however, pointed to Cunningham’s history of defending Clark when she has been targeted around the league. For that reason, some fans simply suggested that she may have overthought the question, or that she genuinely was too busy to watch the final.

The next meeting between Cunningham, Clark and Boston is not far away, which could put some of the fan theories to rest. Indiana is still looking to secure home-court advantage in the first round of the playoffs.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark gives Fever teammates unreleased Caitlin 1s and their reactions become Nike’s best ad
articles.standfirst: The joyful unboxing showed how one generous gesture can create the kind of organic publicity money cannot easily buy
articles.summary: The joyful unboxing showed how one generous gesture can create the kind of organic publicity money cannot easily buy
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark had no intention of advertising her first signature shoes. She simply wanted to do something kind for her Indiana Fever teammates, gifting them pairs of the Nike Caitlin 1 without expecting their reactions to also become “organic” promotional content. And these are players who share a locker room with her every day.

The players expressed their gratitude in different ways. One jumped and celebrated, while another held the shoe like a smartphone and pretended to take a call. It was an unexpected reaction to a gift they never saw coming, but their expressions said everything.

Tyasha Harris described the surprise perfectly: “Christmas came early.”

The moment represents another fulfilled promise from the eight-year, $28 million contract Clark signed with Nike in 2024 . The company has already introduced her personal logo, released apparel and special Kobe-style editions , and finally created the signature shoe included in that historic agreement.

What makes the Nike Caitlin 1 different?

The Caitlin 1 officially launches worldwide on October 1 for $140. It features an Opticast upper designed to improve lateral movement, an Air Zoom Turbo unit and full-length Cushlon foam for responsive cushioning. The double Swoosh forms Clark’s “CC” initials, while her No. 22 appears throughout the design.

Nike designed the shoe around three elements of Clark’s game: a quicker first step, greater separation on her step-back and a faster shot release. It places her alongside other Nike stars with signature models, including Sabrina Ionescu and A’ja Wilson, while Angel Reese has entered the same competitive market with Reebok.

No verified sales figures are publicly available because the general release has not yet taken place, although preorders reportedly sold out in less than 24 hours . The real commercial test still lies ahead: maintaining strong global sales and releasing future Caitlin models throughout the remaining years of her contract.

Clark returns to Indiana as a world champion after Team USA defeated France 97-79 in the FIBA World Cup final. She scored 12 points in 13 minutes and averaged 7.8 points and 5.3 assists during the tournament.

The experience also revealed a more relaxed side of her relationships with Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers. They trained, laughed and celebrated together, leaving old rivalry narratives behind. Clark has now returned to her Fever teammates with a gold medal and a personal gift bearing her own name.

articles.body:
T he Nike Caitlin 1 will not officially arrive in stores until October 1, but Caitlin Clark’s first signature shoe is already becoming difficult to miss.

Her Indiana Fever teammates received pairs before the official retail launch, and several have already worn them during practice. Their excitement and joy while opening the boxes also gave Nike something far more valuable than a traditional advertisement: authentic promotion from the players who share a locker room with Caitlin.

Nike is creating more than one Caitlin Clark shoe

Nike has prepared six colorways for the final months of 2026 : Caitlin Blue, Warning Code, Midnight Fever, Cave Stone, Ice Cold and Purple Venom. Each design connects with a different aspect of Clark’s personality, career or playing style.

Another version, the Friendship Bracelet, was inspired by Taylor Swift and the bracelet-exchanging tradition associated with her Eras Tour. That connection has allowed the Caitlin 1 to transcend basketball and attract attention from fashion outlets, sneaker collectors and Swift fans known as Swifties.

The $140 shoe features Nike’s Opticast upper, an Air Zoom Turbo unit and full-length Cushlon cushioning. It was designed around Clark’s quick first step, step-back separation and fast shooting release. It also includes personal details such as her initials, No. 22 and hidden motivational messages.

There are still no verified public sales figures because the worldwide launch has not yet taken place. That will be the true commercial test, but Nike has already achieved something important: Caitlin Clark’s first signature shoe is everywhere before most fans have even had an opportunity to buy it.

articles.summary: The Friendship Bracelet edition connects two of America’s biggest stars, but Nike has not announced when it will reach stores
articles.body:
The Nike Caitlin 1 will officially launch worldwide on October 1 for $140, but one of its most eye-catching versions could be much harder to obtain. The “Friendship Bracelet” edition was created as a tribute to Taylor Swift and the colorful tradition that emerged during her hugely successful Eras Tour.

The shoe features an off-white upper with soft pink, blue and yellow accents. Its fuzzy laces include customizable beads displaying Clark’s initials and No. 22, recreating the bracelets that Swifties exchange at concerts.

Why Taylor Swift inspired Caitlin Clark’s exclusive shoe

Clark is a devoted Taylor Swift fan. She attended two Eras Tour concerts in Indianapolis and described the show as the best she had ever seen. The friendship bracelet tradition was inspired by a lyric from Swift’s song “You’re on Your Own, Kid” and became one of the tour’s most recognizable symbols.

The admiration is mutual. Swift previously sent Clark gifts and a personal note describing the basketball star as “inspiring to watch from afar.” The two later spent time together while supporting the Kansas City Chiefs , turning their connection into something more than distant celebrity admiration.

New practice images show Clark and several Indiana Fever teammates wearing different Caitlin 1 models after she surprised them with multiple pairs. Their excitement has helped turn the unreleased sneakers into a form of organic advertising for Nike.

Clark has already worn the “Friendship Bracelet” edition during practice, but Nike has not officially confirmed a public release date for this special colorway. For now, the Taylor Swift-inspired Caitlin 1 retains the quality that makes it even more desirable: it is a shoe everyone can see but, at least for now, nobody can buy.

articles.title: Is the WNBA Ignoring Caitlin Clark? Former ESPN anchor denounces treatment of Indiana Fever star
articles.standfirst: WNBA urged to lean into Caitlin Clark after latest promotional backlash
articles.summary: WNBA urged to lean into Caitlin Clark after latest promotional backlash
articles.body:
Linda Cohn believes the WNBA is overcomplicating its relationship with Caitlin Clark . The former ESPN host says Clark’s popularity should be treated as an asset the league can build around, not something it needs to balance so carefully that the Indiana Fever guard occasionally appears sidelined in its own promotion.

Cohn made that case during a recent conversation with journalist Christine Brennan , arguing that the WNBA can spotlight Clark while still respecting the stars and veterans who established the league long before her arrival.

“I was just talking, rehashing with Dominic about it, when the league went out of their way not to promote Caitlin Clark, and because they were so intent of like, ‘Oh, we can’t forget the people that build this,’” Cohn said.

“And I always said you can promote the league through Caitlin Clark,” Cohn continued. “Don’t go out of your way to ignore Caitlin Clark.”

Gateway to the rest of the WNBA

Cohn compared Clark ’s impact to Tiger Woods ’ transformational influence on golf.

“You know, like with Tiger Woods and the PGA Tour many moons ago, she’s making your world better,” she said.

That comparison gets to the heart of the argument. Woods became the sport’s biggest attraction without erasing the achievements of the golfers who preceded him.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham claims WNBA star "literally plays like a dude" in unusual compliment
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever player truly has no filter.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever player truly has no filter.
articles.body:
It's pretty clear that Sophie Cunningham doesn't have much of a filter. She says exactly what's on her mind, regardless of what people might think of her.

While that has earned her many new fans, it has also gotten her into quite a bit of trouble. Her comments on transgender athletes this summer stand out in particular, as she very much divided the sports world on the polarizing topic.

In the meantime, Cunningham has kept chugging along as a key role player for the Indiana Fever . Given her outspoken nature, Cunningham uses her on-court experiences to shed a light on the WNBA through her own lens , particularly on podcasts.

Sophie Cunningham is a big fan of Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles

While doing so this week with sports talk show host Colin Cowherd , Cunningham delivered somewhat odd but also highly complimentary praise for Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles , who she says " plays like a dude ".

You really see the athleticism really changing. People can dunk. People are fast as hell and it's like Olivia Miles. She is a rookie. Like she's killing it and she literally plays like a dude and that is no disrespect. Like that is one of the highest compliments you can ever get.

Due to Cunningham's previous comments on transgender athletes, her compliment of Miles raised some eyebrows. But she meant it in the most flattering of ways: Miles is playing at a level above almost everyone else in the WNBA at the moment .

articles.standfirst: The WNBA returns after the Women's Basketball World Cup for its final games of the regular season.
articles.summary: The WNBA returns after the Women's Basketball World Cup for its final games of the regular season.
articles.body:
The WNBA 2026 postseason is on the horizon , and Atlanta's Gateway Center Arena will be the stage for a clash with opposite scripts.

The Atlanta Dream, master and ruler of the Conference

This game opens the series against a Connecticut Sun team with one of the worst records in the entire league. On paper, there are few games with such a stark contrast. On the court, however, basketball always demands that the game be played.

What time does Angel Reese's game with the Atlanta Dream start today?

The meeting is scheduled for the evening of Thursday , September 17, 2026 at 7:30 pm Eastern Time (6:30 pm Central Time, 4:30 pm Pacific Time) at the Gateway Center Arena in Atlanta, an intimate venue with a capacity of 3,500 spectators that usually becomes a pressure cooker when the Dream is on.

To watch it on TV and streaming, these are your options:

TV Channel: NBC Sports Boston, Peachtree TV

Streaming: WNBA League Pass

How are the Connecticut Sun and Atlanta Dream approaching tonight's game?

The standings are a clear picture. The Atlanta Dream leads the Eastern Conference with a record of 26 wins and 14 losses, the same number of wins as the Indiana Fever , but with the advantage of higher seeding that keeps them at the top.

At the global level of the WNBA, the Dream occupies an enviable fourth place, sustained by one of the most productive offenses in the circuit: 3,632 points scored against 3,428 received, for a difference of +204.

Meanwhile, the outlook for the Connecticut Sun is bleak. The New England team is second to last in the East with 10 wins and 30 losses, and in the league standings they have plummeted to 14th out of 15.

The numbers explain why: they've conceded 3,511 points and only scored 3,158, leaving them with the worst point differential in the entire competition, a devastating -353. Every night, generating points has been a nightmare for the Sun, and visiting a league leader on their home court is hardly the scenario to reverse the trend.

Star-studded duel: the figures who make the difference in the squads

The Dream boasts a roster with hierarchy and well-distributed talent. On the perimeter, Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard form one of the most feared shooting guard duos in the East, capable of punishing opponents from three-point range and attacking the rim. The veteran DeWanna Bonner , at 39 years old, brings experience and game awareness, while point guard Jordin Canada orchestrates the offense with composure.

But the media spotlight is on Angel Reese . The 24-year-old power forward is a rebounding and energy machine in the paint, and her presence under the boards often tips the scales in the paint. Despite their inconsistent season, Connecticut is not lacking in talent. The 35-year-old center Brittney Griner remains a formidable presence in the paint thanks to her size and shot-blocking ability, and Canadian Aaliyah Edwards adds strength in the post.

In the backcourt, young Saniya Rivers represents the future of the project, and New Zealander Charlisse Leger-Walker will try to inject pace into the visitors' attack. The problem for the Sun is clear: their talent hasn't been enough to sustain results throughout a long and grueling season.

Implications for WNBA Playoff Qualification

For Atlanta, every win is worth its weight in gold in their fight to maintain their lead in the East against a hot-footed Indiana Fever (both 26-14) and a threatening New York Liberty . Maintaining their lead and, with it, home-court advantage in the playoffs, is the Dream's top priority at this stage.

Connecticut, meanwhile, enters this game with their season already decided in the lower part of the standings. With a 10-30 record, the Sun are fighting to avoid finishing the season at the bottom of the league and to continue developing their young core for the future.

Connecticut Sun vs Atlanta Dream Prediction

Everything points to a home-court advantage. The Atlanta Dream are playing at home, leading their conference, and boasting a far superior offense against the worst defense in the East . Connecticut would need a perfect night—control of the tempo, accurate outside shooting, and a great performance from Griner in the paint—to pose a threat.

The Dream will most likely showcase their talent and extend their lead as the quarters progress. Atlanta will win comfortably.
