articles.standfirst: After her participation in the Women's Basketball World Cup, Paige Bueckers returns to her team who now face Los Angeles
articles.summary: After her participation in the Women's Basketball World Cup, Paige Bueckers returns to her team who now face Los Angeles
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA schedule opens its first day with a duel full of young talent and curiosity: the Dallas Wings host the Los Angeles Sparks at the College Park Center in Arlington.

It's Matchday 1 after the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup , a clean slate for two franchises that, according to the previous season's standings, finished fourth and sixth in the Western Conference . Both face the same question heading into this new season: can they transform a roster full of perimeter players into a team with its own identity?

Los Angeles Sparks vs Dallas Wings: Schedule and where to watch the game

The game between Dallas and Los Angeles is scheduled for Thursday, September 17, 2026, at 8:00 pm ET (7:00 pm CT and 5:00 pm PT). The venue is the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas , a 7,000-seat arena that provides the Wings with a compact and noisy atmosphere.

To follow the game live, the WNBA broadcast locally will be through KCWX+ Plus, with the option of streaming via WNBA League Pass for those who don't want to miss a thing.

The previous scenario: two offensives to arm

The Dallas Wings built their last season around a handful of dominant scorers. They finished with a 24-16 record, fourth in the West, with 3,560 points for and 3,414 against: a solid offensive record that, nevertheless, left room for improvement on defense.

The Sparks , meanwhile, finished with 15 wins and 25 losses, sixth in the conference, with a point differential of -178, highlighting the Californians' biggest challenge: stopping their opponents. They allowed 3,672 points, one of the most forgiving records in the West.

Both franchises enter this opening stretch with young, mobile rosters, full of guards. The question is who will impose their rhythm first.

The matchup to watch: young point guards with experience

In Dallas, the spotlight is on the backcourt. Paige Bueckers and Arike Ogunbowale form one of the most electrifying guard duos in the league, with Azzi Fudd adding outside shooting and Aziaha James providing energy off the bench.

It's a team that runs, shoots threes, and can overwhelm any defense that lets its guard down. Around them, the veteran presence of Alysha Clark and Odyssey Sims provides experience, while post players Alanna Smith and Jessica Shepard anchor the paint.

The Sparks respond with their own blend of youth and experience. Dearica Hamby anchors the post, supported by the return of Cameron Brink, the big man expected to make a difference on the boards and in the paint.

On the perimeter, Ariel Atkins and veteran Erica Wheeler provide control and scoring, while young players like Chance Gray and Tonie Morgan are looking for minutes and a leading role. It's a roster in the midst of a rebuild that needs to gel quickly.

Key tactical insights for the Los Angeles Sparks vs Dallas Wings game

The game will likely be decided on two fronts. First, the pace: Dallas wants to play fast and punish from beyond the arc with Bueckers, Ogunbowale, and Fudd. If they manage to increase the tempo, Los Angeles's permissive defense—the most punished in the West with 3,672 points allowed—could suffer greatly.

The second front is the paint. There, the Sparks have Hamby and Brink to contest rebounds and protect the rim, neutralizing the Texas guards' penetration. If Brink stays healthy and active near the basket, the game could become a clash of styles: the Wings' speed and outside shooting against the Sparks' size and physicality.

What is the prediction for the Los Angeles Sparks vs Dallas Wings game?

With home-court advantage, depth of talent on the perimeter, and a more experienced core, the Dallas Wings are the favorites going into this opener. The speed and outside shooting of Bueckers and Ogunbowale should weigh heavily against a Sparks defense that was the most permissive in the West last season. Even so, the size of Hamby and Brink keeps the visitors' hopes alive. A high-scoring, fast-paced game is expected, with Dallas winning by a narrow margin in their home opener.

articles.title: Can Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese play together on the Indiana Fever after what we've seen on the U.S. national team?
articles.standfirst: The two adversaries may become teammates when it comes to representing the United States.
articles.summary: The two adversaries may become teammates when it comes to representing the United States.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese spent years at the center of one of women’s basketball’s biggest rivalries, but their time together with Team USA offered a very different picture - and their chemistry has even sparked calls for the pair to share a WNBA court. One hypothetical scenario would see the Indiana Fever trade Aliyah Boston , the 2024 No. 1 overall pick, to acquire Reese but an expert made clear she does not expect such a move anytime soon.

“I don’t think that this is going to happen anytime soon,” Rachel DeMita said to the Courtside Club. “Caitlin and Angel actually playing on the same team, like maybe later on in their career. “And maybe that’s something that we have to look forward to. Whether you’re a huge fan of Angel or a huge fan of Caitlin or you hate the other, you have to admit. There was really something special that they had on the court.” DeMita believes fans may have to wait before seeing Clark and Reese together at the WNBA level but admits their Team USA partnership showed why the idea is so appealing. Clark recorded 32 assists across six FIBA World Cup games, with seven finding Reese and their familiarity appeared to translate naturally onto the court. “Their chemistry was so good,” DeMita added. “Their court awareness of one another… “It’s like they somehow, and maybe it’s because they’ve studied each other’s game, they knew where each other was.”

The dream pairing would also have to account for what the Fever already have in Boston as their current pair have developed an effective pick-and-roll partnership, while Clark ’s shooting threat regularly creates room around the basket. The pair also made WNBA history by becoming the first teammates to each record a 30-point double-double in the same game and that production helps explain why replacing Boston with Reese is far more complicated than fans dream. Simply reuniting two familiar stars is appealing but the Fever are 26-14 and enjoying good chemistry as they lead the Eastern Conference , but Clark and Reese nevertheless appeared to grow closer throughout Team USA ’s FIBA World Cup run. They were seen sitting together during the final round, laughing and bonding as their old college rivalry gave way to a new partnership and After Team USA defeated France for the gold medal, Clark even said she and Reese had always been friends.

Clark dips out of WNBA Top 3 rankings

Meanwhile Clark ’s individual standing remains another storyline heading into the WNBA Playoffs as she continues to develop into the all-conquering star she was tipped to become from college. Despite helping Indiana produce the most prolific offense in league history during a spectacular second half, she placed fifth in Bleacher Report ’s updated Top 25 WNBA rankings. A’ja Wilson topped that list, followed by Olivia Miles , Breanna Stewart and Clark ’s Fever teammate Kelsey Mitchell but the star herself appeared as low as fifth, missing out on the top four entirely. That is despite Clark averaging 22.5 points, 8.4 assists and 3.9 rebounds while shooting 45.6 percent from the field as her impact extends beyond the box score. Her range and passing forcing defenses to react far beyond the arc. Her improved pull-up shooting and floater have also added new dimensions to an already difficult matchup as the Fever prepare for the postseason.

articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark is set to return with the Indiana Fever after a three-week WNBA break, but her injury status remains the biggest storyline.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark is set to return with the Indiana Fever after a three-week WNBA break, but her injury status remains the biggest storyline.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever return to action this Friday against the Toronto Tempo, but the main focus will be on Caitlin Clark ’s physical condition after a three-week break in the WNBA season.

The game will also mark the return of Indiana’s star and center Aliyah Boston , both coming off gold medals with Team USA at the World Cup in Berlin . The two players were key figures in the United States’ dominant run, as the team won every game except one by double digits.

Over the past few weeks, however, one of the biggest storylines surrounding the Fever has been Clark’s health. She has appeared consistently on injury reports due to a lingering back issue.

With the league restarting, the central question is whether Indiana’s biggest star will be ready to perform at the elite level that has made her one of the best players of the season.

Caitlin Clark listed on Fever injury report

Indiana released its first injury report since the season resumed, and Clark was again listed with a back injury. Despite that, the point guard was labeled probable for the matchup against Toronto .

Clark has appeared on injury reports for the past two months, but all signs point to her being available to return to the court. Before wrapping up her participation in the World Cup, she said she felt better than she had in a long time.

Damiris Dantas was also listed as NWT (out) and will not play. The veteran underwent knee surgery and is sidelined for the remainder of the season.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark looks back at her 15-year-old self after carrying Team USA’s historic legacy
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star explained why representing her country at the World Cup meant much more than simply winning another championship
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star explained why representing her country at the World Cup meant much more than simply winning another championship
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark was only 15 years old when she first experienced what it meant to wear the USA Basketball jersey. Nearly a decade later, she stood on basketball’s biggest international stage with a gold medal and a much deeper understanding of the responsibility she had inherited or at least that was how it felt to her.

After helping the United States win the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup , the Indiana Fever’s No. 22 reflected on how difficult it is to earn a place on the national team. The opportunity did not come to her on her first attempt. She also spoke about the pride and determination she saw in opponents representing their countries when the U.S. faced France, Spain, Italy and host nation Germany.

Caitlin Clark helps preserve Team USA’s legacy

“It’s so hard to have this opportunity and represent the people of our country,” Clark said. For her, playing for Team USA meant honoring the generations of women who established a standard that every new group is expected to preserve.

The United States defeated France 97-79 in the final after trailing by 14 points during the second quarter. Clark scored 12 points and made a crucial three-pointer that helped cut the deficit to two before halftime, allowing the Americans to take control after the break.

The victory gave Team USA its fifth consecutive World Cup title and extended an extraordinary 20-year unbeaten run across Olympic and World Cup competition. Clark described preserving that legacy as one of basketball’s most difficult challenges, even comparing the demands of the World Cup with those of the Olympic Games .

Clark had already played in sold-out arenas and carried enormous expectations throughout her college and WNBA careers, but representing her country brought a different kind of pressure and an emotion that cannot be experienced in just any tournament.

Her message after winning gold was simple and direct: opportunities like this do not come around often, the legacy belongs to an entire team and transcends any individual player, and moments like these should never be taken for granted; they must be lived to be truly felt.

articles.title: Angel Reese puts her adventure with Caitlin Clark behind her to dominate the WNBA once again
articles.standfirst: After weeks of Caitlin Clark headlines, Angel Reese let her game do all the talking.
articles.summary: After weeks of Caitlin Clark headlines, Angel Reese let her game do all the talking.
articles.body:
A ngel Reese scored 30 points on 11-of-14 shooting and had 10 rebounds to help the Atlanta Dream rout the Connecticut Sun 103-59 on Thursday night in the first WNBA game following a nearly three-week break for the FIBA World Cup .

A key member of the winning U.S. team in Germany, Reese reached 30 points on a free throw with 5:38 remaining and grabbed her 10th rebound a few seconds later for her WNBA-record 30th double-double of the season . She finished a point shy of her career high, playing 25 minutes in the blowout for the playoff-bound Dream.

Rhyne Howard set a WNBA season record with 129 3-pointers . She made her only 3-pointer of the game — in nine attempts — with 6:45 left in the fourth to break Sabrina Ionescu’s record set in 2023 — reaching the mark in just 40 games.

Howard finished with 10 points. Allisha Gray also had 10 for Atlanta (27-14) to break her own franchise record for points in a season with 782.

Olivia Nelson-Ododa led Connecticut (10-31) with 13 points — all in the first half. Connecticut was outscored 31-11 in the third and 27-13 in the fourth.

Reese made a 3-pointer from the corner midway through the third for her 10th field goal in 13 attempts. It was it 61-40 following a 16-5 run.

Atlanta announced before the game that Brionna Jones would miss the remainder of the season due to a left leg injury suffered Aug. 13.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham weighs in on ad featuring nude Sydney Sweeney and doesn't hold back: “That's what she's known for”
articles.standfirst: Cunningham pushed back on the anger surrounding Sweeney's ad
articles.summary: Cunningham pushed back on the anger surrounding Sweeney's ad
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham ’s reaction to Sydney Sweeney ’s much-discussed Novig advertisement came with criticism, skepticism and, ultimately, a defense of the actress’s right to do what she wants.

The Indiana Fever guard addressed the ad on her “No Hesitation” podcast with Drew Hanlen after saying she had been flooded with requests to comment on it.

Sweeney ’s campaign for sports prediction platform Novig showed the actress posing nude while covered by sports equipment.

The ad quickly sparked debate over whether the concept undercut the progress women’s sports has made in being marketed around athletic performance rather than appearance.

Cunningham ’s first reaction focused on whether Sweeney had any genuine connection to the product.

“I have so many takes, but first of all, does she even gamble on sports? Like, it's just so inauthentic,” Cunningham said.

“I really like her and you know what? She sticks to her guns and she does her thing and she's her,” Cunningham added. “So, like props to her.”

Cunningham offers opinion on Sweeney

Cunningham made clear that the campaign itself wasn't something she would endorse.

“Do I like it? Like that particular ad? Not really,” she said. “I think it's like, I mean like what are we doing? But again, I'm not surprised. She's making her money. Go do your thing, sis.”

Cunningham also questioned why the backlash had become so intense, arguing that the concept was hardly inconsistent with Sweeney ’s public image.

“But why are girls mad?” she said. “Like that is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad?”

She continued: “Men. Sports. Pretty much naked women. Like of course that's going to draw attention.”

Cunningham said she found the ad “kind of weird” from a moral perspective, but repeatedly returned to the idea that Sweeney should be allowed to make her own choices.

Fever guard turns debate toward women athletes

The conversation eventually moved away from Sweeney and toward body image in women’s sports.

Cunningham spoke about growing up taller than many girls and learning to take pride in the physical traits that come with being an athlete.

“I think it has been so cool to see girls who, you know what, they're muscly, their thighs touch, they have broad shoulders, they might be taller than the average girl and probably the average boy,” she said.

“But you know what? I think that's what it is. You've got to embrace your power.”

Cunningham also acknowledged why the Novig ad may have frustrated some women athletes.

“I can understand when you first see that ad that like it could kind of deflate women, because we've worked so hard to get a little bit of respect around here,” she said.

Her final position, though, was less about condemnation than acceptance: “But then when you really think about it, it's like screw it, let that girl go do her thing.”

articles.title: Paige Bueckers is on the verge of rewriting WNBA history just two seasons into her career
articles.standfirst: Bueckers and the Wings improved from finishing last season in last place to making the playoffs this year
articles.summary: Bueckers and the Wings improved from finishing last season in last place to making the playoffs this year
articles.body:
The WNBA is back after the FIBA Women's World Cup tournament in which Team USA won the gold medal against France in the final.

In the WNBA, the eight teams already qualified for the playoffs are competing for finishing in a better position on the standings, and on last night's games, the four teams qualified, Atlanta Dream , Washington Mystics , Las Vegas Aces , and Dallas Wings , won their matchups.

Aside from the standings, the other critical storyline centers around the major annual awards: for MVP , four-time winner A'ja Wilson stands as the heavy favorite over Indiana Fever stars Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell .

Meanwhile, for the Rookie of the Year race, the clear winner is second overall pick Olivia Miles , marking the first time since 2021 that the number one overall selection will not capture the prestigious rookie honor.

Paige Bueckers Chases Seimone Augustus' Historic Two-Year WNBA Scoring Record

Olivia Miles has pieced together a historic maiden campaign, averaging 19.7 PPG and 6.0 APG , leading her squad while ranking inside the top eight across the entire association.

Focusing on Bueckers, the Dallas Wings guard recently chipped in 19 points during a dominant 97-77 victory over the Los Angeles Sparks. Following that output, the talented second-year player needs just 25 more points across her final three regular-season games to etch her name permanently into the record books.

Averaging a modest 8.3 points per game over her last trio of contests would officially grant Bueckers the WNBA record for the most total points scored by any player through their first two professional seasons.

That milestone is currently held by Seimone Augustus , who accumulated 1,513 points with an average of 22.3 PPG across the 2006 and 2007 seasons.

Paige's career average sits slightly lower at 19.9 PPG , though she has already logged heavier durability, appearing in 75 WNBA games compared to Augustus' 68 matches during that same initial timeframe.

While this two-year scoring milestone is practically locked up for Bueckers, that specific benchmark could face an immediate challenge next season from Miles, provided she maintains her health.

The surging Wings can cap off their schedule with an impressive eight-game winning streak if they sweep their final three contests against eliminated opponents, playing Phoenix twice and closing out the regular season next Wednesday against the Seattle Storm.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham gets vulnerable about what makes her different and how she uses it to succeed
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star returned for Season 2 of Beyond Basketball with a deeply personal message
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star returned for Season 2 of Beyond Basketball with a deeply personal message
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has built her career by refusing to hide her irreverent and, when necessary, confrontational personality. Now, the Indiana Fever star wants the next generation to understand that being different is not something they need to overcome. In fact, it could become their greatest strength.

“Embrace what makes you different than everyone else because that’s going to be your biggest superpower,” Cunningham said. “Being you is what’s going to set you apart and make you successful.”

The message became one of the defining moments from the first episode of the second season of Beyond Basketball with Sophie Cunningham , presented by Yrefy.

Cunningham and several special guests visited a local farm for a conversation that went far beyond what happens on a basketball court. They discussed personal branding, the importance of investing and the responsibility of inspiring the young people following their journeys, all while enjoying the farm’s unique surroundings.

Sophie Cunningham turns her differences into an advantage

The farm proved to be a meaningful setting for Cunningham. The WNBA guard grew up in Missouri and has often spoken about how her family, her Midwestern upbringing and the time she spent around farms helped shape her personality. She understands that environment well and knows how to handle whatever situations may arise with the animals.

That background has always distinguished her from many professional athletes, but Cunningham has never attempted to hide it. Her direct opinions, competitive attitude and willingness to show her authentic personality have helped make her one of the WNBA’s most recognizable players without forcing her to stop being herself.

Building a personal brand requires people to understand what separates them from everyone else, while investing can provide the financial foundation needed to transform short-term success into long-term stability.

For young athletes, those lessons can be particularly valuable. A playing career can change suddenly because of an injury, a roster decision or circumstances beyond their control. Creating an identity and making thoughtful financial decisions can help prepare them for whatever comes next.

Cunningham experienced that uncertainty when a knee injury ended her 2025 season early. She returned to the Indiana Fever for a second season in 2026, but the setback reminded her once again that an athlete’s identity and future cannot depend entirely on basketball. Beyond Basketball gives Cunningham an opportunity to explore those broader conversations.

Young people do not need to erase their differences to become successful . According to Cunningham, embracing and even highlighting those qualities may be exactly what helps them stand out while feeling more confident and less vulnerable about showing others who they truly are.

Some basketballs appear close to the rim, while many others spread across the perimeter and beyond the 3-point line. The image demonstrates the problem facing opposing defenses: Clark and Mitchell can threaten them from almost anywhere on the court.

Clark creates pressure with her extraordinary range, passing and ability to control the offense. Mitchell adds speed, movement without the ball and one of the most consistent scoring touches in the WNBA . Defending one can create the small opening the other needs.

Clark’s range and vision make Mitchell more dangerous, while Mitchell’s constant movement creates additional space for Clark . articles.standfirst: After several weeks away from the action with Indiana Fever, the player returned just as the season enters its decisive stretch.
articles.summary: After several weeks away from the action with Indiana Fever, the player returned just as the season enters its decisive stretch.
articles.body:
There was something special about seeing Sophie Cunningham back on the court with Indiana Fever. The player had not participated in the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup , and her return to the team came after a break that had kept the WNBA waiting.

This time, her appearance started long before tip-off.

Sophie Cunningham arrived in Toronto in one of her most eye-catching looks

On September 18, Indiana visited the Toronto Tempo at Coca-Cola Coliseum to resume the regular season .

Before the game, Cunningham showed up wearing formal white pants, a cropped gray top, white heels, a cross pendant necklace and her hair down . The combination had all the elements that often make her arrivals at the arena part of the conversation around her.

She didn’t need the uniform to make it clear that her return also came with a bit of style.

Then, it was time to get back to what mattered: playing.

Sophie was back in action

Cunningham came off the bench and played 20 minutes against Toronto. She finished the night with 5 points, 4 rebounds and 1 assist , while Indiana put together one of its more comfortable offensive performances of the game.

The Fever won 103-85 . Kelsey Mitchell led the team with 25 points, while Caitlin Clark finished with a double-double of 15 points and 11 assists.

Now comes the most important part of the season

The game against Toronto came with Indiana already having mathematically secured its spot in the WNBA playoffs. At this point, the goal over the final games is no longer simply to make the postseason, but to determine the position in which the Fever will enter it.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham responds sharply to criticism for not watching the US national team's World Cup matches
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard explained why she was not watching the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup final after her NASCAR appearance drew criticism online
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard explained why she was not watching the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup final after her NASCAR appearance drew criticism online
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has pushed back against criticism over her decision not to watch the United States' FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup final against France, insisting that her absence from the broadcast did not mean she was indifferent to the team or her Indiana Fever teammates.

The controversy began after Cunningham attended the NASCAR Enjoy Illinois 300 at World Wide Technology Raceway in Illinois on September 13, the same day Team USA faced France for the gold medal.

Cunningham was working at the event as a USA Network studio analyst and spent time around several prominent figures from the motorsport world, including Michael Jordan and Jeff Gordon .

When she was asked the following day whether she had watched Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston play for Team USA, Cunningham gave a brief response: “No, I was busy.”

After being informed that the United States had beaten France and that Clark and Boston had "got it done," Cunningham replied: “Good! Congrats,”

That response quickly circulated online, with some fans questioning why a Fever player would not have watched two of her teammates compete for a gold medal.

Cunningham has now offered considerably more context on her No Hesitation podcast, explaining that she had been following the tournament even though she was not sitting down to watch the final.

“I definitely saw the stats,” she said on the podcast.

She then described the repeated questions she received about whether she had watched the game.

“I knew they won gold. Some guy was like, ‘So did you watch the game?’ And I was like, ‘No.’ And they’re like, ‘Well, they won gold.’ And I’m like, ‘Duh, they won gold.’ Like, you don’t think that I’m not invested in, first of all, USA, on any sport, I’m going to be tracking. And then like, if my coach is there and my two teammates, I’m dialed in, but people are just dumb, dumb, dumb, dumb.”

Cunningham's NASCAR appearance created an awkward comparison

The timing of the NASCAR assignment made the situation particularly noticeable. Cunningham was not simply away from basketball during the World Cup final; she was actively appearing at another major sporting event.

During the broadcast, she made clear how much the opportunity meant to her.

“We’re here in Illinois with NASCAR,” she said. “It’s been the best day of my entire life. I feel these are my people. I belong here. I’m wearing all-black; I got my leather on, boots on. I’m pulling out my Talladega nights, baby.”

The NASCAR role also gave Cunningham the opportunity to interact with Michael Jordan , a fellow basketball icon who was attending the event in his capacity as co-owner of 23XI Racing.

Meanwhile, Team USA was completing one of the most dominant runs in the history of the women's World Cup. The Americans defeated France 97-79 in the final to win their fifth consecutive World Cup title and 12th overall. The victory also extended the United States' World Cup winning streak to 36 games.

Clark played a significant role throughout the tournament despite coming off the bench. She averaged 7.8 points and a team-leading 5.3 assists per game, while Boston contributed primarily through her defense and averaged 6.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, 0.8 steals and 0.5 blocks.

Indiana also had representation on the coaching staff. Fever head coach Stephanie White served as an assistant to Team USA head coach Kara Lawson.

White subsequently praised Clark's performance during a Fever practice.

“It was really great,” she told reporters.

“You could tell the way she was able to change the game with her pace…I thought her floor game was outstanding. I mean, the way that she got everybody involved was outstanding. And you could see her confidence continue to grow as the tournament progressed. And that shot that she hit right before halftime against France was a momentum-changing shot. She stepped up, and she knocked it down.”

Cunningham's clarification arrives as Indiana prepares for the final stretch of the WNBA regular season. The Fever entered the final week with a 26-14 record and a playoff position already secured, with four games remaining on the schedule.

Her explanation does not change the fact that she missed the live broadcast of the gold-medal game, but she clearly wants to distinguish that decision from a lack of interest in Team USA.

For Cunningham , the message is straightforward: she was working at another sporting event, followed the result and knew exactly what had happened. With the Fever's postseason push now approaching, her attention has returned to Indiana and the team's remaining games.

articles.title: Can Caitlin Clark win her first WNBA title? Kelsey Mitchell is a big reason why
articles.standfirst: The consistency the Indiana Fever has shown may be even more remarkable
articles.summary: The consistency the Indiana Fever has shown may be even more remarkable
articles.body:
T he Indiana Fever may not be the betting favorite to win the WNBA championship, but they have something every contender covets entering the postseason: an elite offensive duo capable of taking over a game. Caitlin Clark is the face of the franchise and one of the league’s biggest stars, but if Indiana is going to make a serious run at its first championship since 2012, Kelsey Mitchell may be the player who ultimately determines how far the Fever can go.

Mitchell delivered another reminder of her importance Friday night, erupting for 33 points in a 103-85 victory over the Toronto Tempo . The performance was historic in multiple ways. During the game, she surpassed the single-season scoring mark of 1,021 points set by A'ja Wilson in 2024, establishing a new WNBA record with 1,034 points and counting.

As impressive as the record was, the consistency may be even more remarkable. Mitchell has now scored at least 20 points in 25 consecutive games, extending her own WNBA record. Against Toronto , she was nearly unstoppable, shooting 12-for-17 from the field and knocking down seven of her 11 attempts from beyond the arc.

That kind of offensive firepower changes everything

Clark was excellent as well. Playing in her first game since helping Team USA capture the FIBA Women's World Cup in Germany, the superstar guard finished with 28 points and 14 assists. It marked her 14th double-double of the season and matched her season-high assist total, which she also recorded against Toronto on June 16.

The stat line illustrated what makes Indiana such a dangerous playoff opponent. When Clark is orchestrating the offense at an elite level, defenses are forced to make impossible decisions. Opponents can commit extra attention to Clark and risk leaving Mitchell open , or they can focus on slowing Mitchell and allow Clark to dictate the game as a scorer and playmaker.

Few teams possess two perimeter players capable of punishing defenses in so many different ways. The Fever's recent form suggests the partnership is peaking at the right time. Indiana has won eight of its last 10 games and appears to be building momentum as the regular season enters its final stretch.

The calendar now becomes critical

The WNBA resumed play following the international break, leaving every team with just four regular-season games remaining before the schedule concludes on Sept. 24. The postseason begins three days later on Sept. 27, meaning contenders have little time to build momentum before the intensity of playoff basketball arrives.

That short turnaround places an even greater emphasis on continuity and chemistry. Teams that can quickly regain their rhythm after the W orld Cup interruption could enter the playoffs with a significant advantage. The combination of Clark's playmaking and Mitchell's historic scoring surge gives the Fever reason to believe they can hit the ground running when the postseason opens.

Mitchell's record-breaking campaign has elevated her from All-Star status into the MVP conversation. More importantly for the Fever, it has given Clark the kind of offensive partner every championship contender needs.

The burden of carrying a playoff offense no longer falls solely on Clark's shoulders. On nights when defenses load up against Indiana's superstar point guard, Mitchell has shown she can take over games. On nights when Kelsey attracts extra attention, Caitlin has the vision and passing ability to create opportunities for everyone around her.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham gets upset about a flaw in her pre-game outfit
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham is one of the fashion icons of the WNBA, and her outfits stand out from the rest of the competition with bold choices that fans absolutely love.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham is one of the fashion icons of the WNBA, and her outfits stand out from the rest of the competition with bold choices that fans absolutely love.

But her latest choice before a big game against the Toronto Tempo got her upset, and it was all recorded on video. Sophie chose white long linen pants with a cute grey top.

The problem was that the WNBA star didn’t even wear the pants for the 10 minutes, and they already had a black stain in the back. Talk about bad luck! The good news? Indiana beat Toronto 103-85.
